footnotes: Banks have no cost of sales; the flow chart shows revenue (net interest income + noninterest income) going to noninterest expense and the provision for credit losses, leaving pre-tax income. From pre-tax income to net loss to common: after income tax and $9.4M of preferred dividends & other. Efficiency ratio = noninterest expense ÷ revenue (lower is better).
Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income) fell 13.4% to $325M in 2025. Net interest income rose 0.2% to $237M and noninterest income fell 36.4% to $88.2M; noninterest expense rose 82.8%, and the provision for credit losses was $59.8M, versus $120M.
Net loss to common was −$134M, versus $28.6M, or −$6.12 per diluted share, and the efficiency ratio was 116.9% versus 55.4%. Midland States Bancorp returned $37.3M through dividends and buybacks.
